subject: Cable Trunking and Raceways
rationale: Cable trunking may pass through or be enclosed within wall cavities, though some raceways are surface-mounted on walls.

subject: Cable Basket and Mesh Systems
rationale: In some configurations, cable mesh systems are mounted on walls for cable routing.

subject: Cable Basket and Mesh Systems
rationale: Cable baskets are often located above a suspended/drop ceiling in the plenum space.

subject: Cable Basket and Mesh Systems
rationale: Cable mesh systems are installed at an elevation above the floor slab, either overhead or in raised floors.

subject: Sprinkler Control Valve
rationale: Sprinkler control valves are often located in mechanical rooms or fire protection valve rooms for accessibility by fire safety personnel.

subject: Sprinkler Control Valve
rationale: Flow switches are commonly installed on the same pipe section near the control valve to detect water movement.

subject: Sprinkler Control Valve
rationale: In many configurations, the sprinkler control valve is located above the fire pump in the piping riser system.

subject: Sprinkler Water Supply Connection
rationale: A sprinkler water supply connection is the physical point where the sprinkler system ties into the building's main water supply system.

subject: Sprinkler Water Supply Connection
rationale: If a fire pump is present, the sprinkler water supply connection is typically adjacent to or directly connected to the fire pump intake.

subject: Sprinkler Water Supply Connection
rationale: A backflow preventer is typically installed inline with the sprinkler water supply connection to prevent contamination of the potable water supply.

subject: Sprinkler System Riser
rationale: The sprinkler system riser is the main vertical pipe that connects to the fire suppression system's water supply and distribution network.

subject: Sprinkler System Riser
rationale: The riser typically houses or contains the main control valve for the sprinkler system.

subject: Sprinkler System Riser
rationale: Flow switches are commonly installed on the sprinkler riser to detect water flow.

subject: Sprinkler System Riser
rationale: The sprinkler riser is often located adjacent to or near the fire pump in a fire pump room.

subject: Sprinkler System Riser
rationale: The riser is typically mounted vertically above a floor drain for drainage and testing purposes.

subject: Sprinkler Flow Switch
rationale: The flow switch is typically located along the same pipe branch that feeds sprinkler heads, though not necessarily directly adjacent.

subject: Sprinkler Flow Switch
rationale: Flow switches on main risers are often located in mechanical rooms for maintenance access.

subject: Sprinkler Flow Switch
rationale: Flow switches on branch lines are often installed above ceiling tiles in concealed spaces.

subject: Sprinkler Tamper Switch
rationale: The tamper switch is a component of the sprinkler system, electrically connected to monitor valve position.

subject: Sprinkler Tamper Switch
rationale: Sprinkler tamper switches are often installed above ceilings or in mechanical spaces where sprinkler valves are located.

subject: Sprinkler Tamper Switch
rationale: The tamper switch is typically located within a mechanical room for access to the sprinkler valve.

subject: Sprinkler Drain Valve
rationale: A sprinkler drain valve is a component that connects to the sprinkler system piping to allow drainage of water.

subject: Sprinkler Drain Valve
rationale: Drain valves are often located near the main control valve of the sprinkler system for coordinated operation and maintenance.

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Hanger and Support
rationale: Sprinkler pipe hangers and supports are typically mounted above or within ceiling assemblies to suspend piping.

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Hanger and Support
rationale: Hangers and supports are often anchored to the structural slab or deck above to carry the load of sprinkler pipes.

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Hanger and Support
rationale: Hangers and supports are frequently attached to structural beams for load transfer.

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Hanger and Support
rationale: Hangers and supports are positioned along the pipe run and may be near sprinkler heads, but not directly connected to them.

subject: Sprinkler Pipe Hanger and Support
rationale: In top-floor installations, hangers and supports hang below the roof deck structure.

subject: Sprinkler Escutcheon
rationale: The sprinkler escutcheon is a decorative trim ring that mounts directly around the sprinkler head, connecting to it physically.

subject: Sprinkler Escutcheon
rationale: The escutcheon is mounted flush against the ceiling surface, providing a finished appearance around the sprinkler head penetration.

subject: Sprinkler Escutcheon
rationale: The escutcheon plate sits within the ceiling opening and is partially recessed into or against the ceiling material.

subject: Sprinkler Head Guard
rationale: The guard is physically attached to or surrounding the sprinkler head itself.

subject: Sprinkler Head Guard
rationale: Sprinkler head guards are installed on ceilings, positioned below the ceiling surface or flush with it.

subject: Sprinkler System Room
rationale: Sprinkler system rooms are typically located adjacent to corridors for easy access and maintenance.

subject: Sprinkler System Room
rationale: Sprinkler system rooms often house the fire pump that pressurizes the sprinkler system.

subject: Sprinkler System Room
rationale: The main control valves for the sprinkler system are located within the sprinkler room.

subject: Sprinkler System Room
rationale: Sprinkler rooms are typically accessible from a main entrance or service corridor for fire department access.

subject: Sprinkler System Room
rationale: Sprinkler system rooms are often located near mechanical rooms for coordination of building services.

subject: Sprinkler System Room
rationale: The sprinkler system room is enclosed by the building's structural walls and slabs.

subject: Metal Stud Framing
rationale: Cavities within metal stud framing often contain insulation material for thermal and acoustic performance.

subject: Metal Stud Framing
rationale: Metal stud framing sits above the floor slab or subfloor.

subject: Corner Beads
rationale: Corner beads are typically installed at the external corners of walls to protect the edges and provide a straight corner finish.

subject: Corner Beads
rationale: Corner beads typically run vertically along wall corners and terminate at the ceiling level, thus below the ceiling.

subject: Access Panels and Hatches
rationale: Access panels and hatches are typically installed within or flush against wall surfaces to provide access to hidden utilities.

subject: Access Panels and Hatches
rationale: Ceiling access hatches are installed in ceiling surfaces for access to roof spaces or services above.

subject: Access Panels and Hatches
rationale: Access panels provide connection points to plumbing valves, meters, or cleanouts behind walls or under floors.

subject: Access Panels and Hatches
rationale: Access panels provide connection points to electrical junction boxes, switches, or panels concealed in walls or ceilings.

subject: Access Panels and Hatches
rationale: Access hatches provide connection to HVAC equipment, dampers, or filters located in ceiling plenums or service shafts.

subject: Insulated Sheathing
rationale: Insulated sheathing is placed between the exterior cladding and the structural framing, adjacent to the cladding layer.

subject: Insulated Sheathing
rationale: In a typical building section, insulated sheathing in walls is below the roof assembly.

subject: Insulated Metal Panel
rationale: Insulated metal panels are often installed adjacent to window openings with flashing at the interface.

subject: Insulation Vapor Retarder / Air Barrier
rationale: The vapor retarder/air barrier is typically placed adjacent to insulation layers in building envelope assemblies.

subject: Insulation Vapor Retarder / Air Barrier
rationale: In some assemblies, the vapor retarder/air barrier sits adjacent to or behind the exterior cladding system.

subject: Insulation Vapor Retarder / Air Barrier
rationale: The vapor retarder/air barrier can also be a component enclosed within a roof assembly.

subject: Insulation Vapor Retarder / Air Barrier
rationale: On the interior side, the vapor retarder/air barrier may be adjacent to gypsum board or drywall.

subject: Insulation Vapor Retarder / Air Barrier
rationale: The air barrier connects to window frames to ensure airtightness around openings.

subject: Insulation Vapor Retarder / Air Barrier
rationale: In foundation applications, the vapor retarder/air barrier is placed adjacent to or below concrete slabs.

subject: Insulation Fastening & Accessories
rationale: Fastening systems and accessories are physically placed adjacent to or directly on the insulation layer to secure it.

subject: Insulation Fastening & Accessories
rationale: Fastening accessories may be adjacent to vapor retarder layers depending on the assembly configuration.

subject: Bonded Screed
rationale: Bonded screed is laid directly on top of a concrete slab or substrate to create a smooth floor surface.

subject: Bonded Screed
rationale: Bonded screed is typically adjacent to or directly beneath the final floor finish (e.g., tiles, vinyl, timber).

subject: Bonded Screed
rationale: At the perimeter, bonded screed meets walls, and may be connected via expansion joints or edge strips.

subject: Unbonded Screed
rationale: Unbonded screed sits above the structural slab, with a separating layer in between, so it is positioned above the slab.

subject: Unbonded Screed
rationale: Unbonded screed serves as a base or substrate for the final floor finish (e.g., tiles, wood, carpet), so it is below the floor finish.

subject: Unbonded Screed
rationale: Unbonded screed is typically isolated from walls by perimeter insulation strips, making it adjacent to these strips at the edges.

subject: Unbonded Screed
rationale: Unbonded screed provides a flat surface onto which the floor finish is bonded or laid, forming a connection between the two layers.

subject: Floating Screed
rationale: A floating screed is typically installed below the final floor finish as a leveling and soundproofing layer.

subject: Floating Screed
rationale: Floating screed is laid above the structural concrete slab, often with a separating or insulation layer in between.

subject: Floating Screed
rationale: Floating screed is often placed above thermal or acoustic insulation to ensure the screed floats independently.

subject: Floating Screed
rationale: In some configurations, underfloor heating pipes can be embedded within or laid on top of a floating screed; typically the screed encases or sits below the pipes.

subject: Floating Screed
rationale: The floating screed is separated from surrounding walls by a movement or expansion joint to allow independent movement.

subject: Heated Floor Screed
rationale: Heated floor screed is laid above an insulation layer to minimise downward heat loss.

subject: Heated Floor Screed
rationale: Expansion joints are placed within or adjacent to the screed layer to accommodate thermal movement.

subject: Heated Floor Screed
rationale: The heated screed is typically poured above the structural concrete slab (with insulation in between).

subject: Screed Reinforcement Mesh
rationale: In a typical floor build-up, screed reinforcement mesh sits within the screed below the final floor finish (e.g., tiles, wood, carpet).

subject: Screed Reinforcement Mesh
rationale: In many floor constructions, the screed (with reinforcement mesh) is poured above an insulation or underlayment layer.

subject: Screed Reinforcement Mesh
rationale: Where underfloor heating is present, the screed reinforcement mesh is usually positioned above the heating pipes to reinforce the screed encasing them.

subject: Screed Reinforcement Mesh
rationale: Reinforcement mesh is typically cut or discontinued at expansion joints in the screed, so it is adjacent to but not crossing such joints.

subject: Screed Reinforcement Mesh
rationale: The screed containing the reinforcement mesh is typically bonded or laid on top of the structural concrete slab, transferring loads.

subject: Roof Deck
rationale: Roof decks are typically located on top of a building, positioned above the main structure.

subject: Roof Deck
rationale: Roof decks are commonly accessed via staircases from the floor below.

subject: Roof Edge Flashing / Trim
rationale: Roof edge flashing/trim is typically installed along the perimeter of the roof deck, positioned above it as a finishing layer.

subject: Roof Edge Flashing / Trim
rationale: The flashing overlaps or sits adjacent to the roof membrane along the edges to provide waterproofing.

subject: Roof Edge Flashing / Trim
rationale: Roof edge flashing/trim often connects to or integrates with the fascia board at the roof edge.

subject: Roof Edge Flashing / Trim
rationale: A drip edge is a specific type of roof edge flashing/trim that directs water away from the fascia.

subject: Roof Edge Flashing / Trim
rationale: Roof edge flashing/trim is a component within the overall roof assembly.

subject: Roof Edge Flashing / Trim
rationale: Flashing/trim sits above the top of exterior walls at the roof-wall intersection.

subject: Penetration Flashing
rationale: Penetration flashing is installed around roof penetrations (e.g., pipes, vents), making it adjacent to the roof surface.

subject: Penetration Flashing
rationale: Penetration flashing is installed above the roof deck surface at penetration points.

subject: Expansion Joint Assembly
rationale: Expansion joints are typically placed between adjacent concrete slab sections to accommodate thermal movement.

subject: Expansion Joint Assembly
rationale: Expansion joint assemblies often connect or interface with steel beams where structural movement is accommodated.

subject: Expansion Joint Assembly
rationale: Expansion joints are frequently located adjacent to columns to isolate structural elements and prevent damage from differential movement.

subject: Expansion Joint Assembly
rationale: In building envelopes, expansion joint assemblies may be enclosed by exterior wall systems at building expansion/seismic joint locations.

subject: Roof Curb
rationale: A roof curb is typically installed above the roof surface to support HVAC equipment or other rooftop units.

subject: Roof Curb
rationale: Roof curbs often provide a connection point for ductwork passing through the roof for ventilation or exhaust systems.

subject: Roof Curb
rationale: The roof curb is mounted directly on and adjacent to the roof deck surface.

subject: Roof Curb
rationale: The roof curb is typically flashed and enclosed by the roofing membrane for waterproofing.

subject: Roof Curb
rationale: The roof curb sits above the roof structure and thus above the ceiling plane below.

subject: Roof Curb
rationale: Flashing is installed around the roof curb to create a watertight seal between the curb and the roof membrane.

subject: Skylight / Roof Window
rationale: A skylight or roof window typically contains glazing (glass panel) as its main component.

subject: Skylight / Roof Window
rationale: A skylight/roof window is installed within and contained by the roof structure.

subject: Skylight / Roof Window
rationale: The skylight frame is adjacent to and integrated with surrounding roof structural elements.

subject: Skylight / Roof Window
rationale: Some skylights may connect to ventilation ducts, but this is not universal.

subject: Roof Walkway Pads
rationale: Roof Walkway Pads are installed on top of the roof surface, positioned above the roof membrane and deck.

subject: Roof Walkway Pads
rationale: Walkway pads are typically placed directly on or adjacent to the roof membrane to provide protected walking paths.

subject: Roof Walkway Pads
rationale: The roof walkway pads sit above the roof deck, as the roof structure supports them indirectly via the membrane and insulation layers.

subject: Roof Walkway Pads
rationale: Walkway pads are positioned above the insulation layer, which is part of the roof assembly beneath the walking surface.

subject: Roof Hatch
rationale: A roof hatch typically provides access from the roof deck to the interior of the building or vice versa.

subject: Roof Hatch
rationale: The roof hatch is located above the ceiling plane, as it penetrates the roof assembly.

subject: Roof Hatch
rationale: The roof hatch is physically installed adjacent to and sealed against the roof membrane.

subject: Roof Hatch
rationale: The roof hatch is mounted on and enclosed by a roof curb that transitions through the roof deck.

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rationale: The window frame is a component that is enclosed within the window assembly.

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rationale: The bottom of the window frame rests adjacent to the window sill.

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rationale: The top of the window frame is adjacent to the window head (header).

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rationale: The vertical sides of the window frame are adjacent to the window jambs.

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rationale: In operable windows, the frame contains the sash assembly.

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rationale: The window frame is installed into and connects to the surrounding wall structure.

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rationale: Weatherstripping is applied adjacent to the window frame for sealing.

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rationale: The window frame is positioned above the window sill.

subject: Window Frame (Component)
rationale: The window frame is positioned below the window head.

subject: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
rationale: A window glazing/glass panel is a component part of a larger window assembly or frame system.

subject: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
rationale: The glass panel is typically set into and enclosed by the window frame.

subject: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
rationale: The glazing panel sits adjacent to the sash (the movable part of the window that holds the glass).

subject: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
rationale: The glazing panel is positioned above the window sill within the window opening.

subject: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
rationale: The window glazing (via its frame) connects to the exterior wall as part of the building envelope.

subject: Window Casing / Trim
rationale: Window casing/trim is the decorative frame that sits directly adjacent to the window assembly, surrounding its perimeter.

subject: Window Casing / Trim
rationale: The window casing/trim is installed into and enclosed by the wall opening around the window.

subject: Window Casing / Trim
rationale: The bottom portion of window casing/trim connects to and often overlaps the window sill.

subject: Window Casing / Trim
rationale: The casing/trim typically sits above the window sill, which forms the bottom ledge.

subject: Window Casing / Trim
rationale: Casing/trim is installed directly over the gap between window frame and wall, adjacent to the frame.

subject: Door Casing / Architrave
rationale: Door casing/architrave is the decorative frame that surrounds a door opening, so it is directly adjacent to the door leaf and frame.

subject: Door Casing / Architrave
rationale: The architrave is mounted onto the wall surface around the door opening, effectively being enclosed or supported by the wall.

subject: Door Casing / Architrave
rationale: The architrave is typically attached to the door frame, connecting the frame to the surrounding wall surface.

subject: Door Leaf / Door Slab
rationale: The door leaf/slab is physically mounted within and adjacent to the door frame.

subject: Door Leaf / Door Slab
rationale: Door leaf/slab is connected to the frame via hinges, allowing rotation.

subject: Door Leaf / Door Slab
rationale: The door leaf contacts the door stop when fully closed, limiting its swing.

subject: Door Leaf / Door Slab
rationale: A door closer may be mounted on top of the door leaf for automatic closing; not always present.

subject: Door Leaf / Door Slab
rationale: The door leaf/slab is positioned above the threshold at the bottom of the door opening.

subject: Glazing Bead / Stop
rationale: The glazing bead/stop is a component that physically contacts and holds the glazing panel in place within a window frame.

subject: Glazing Bead / Stop
rationale: The glazing bead/stop is attached to or snapped into the window frame to secure the glass.

subject: Glazing Bead / Stop
rationale: The glazing bead/stop is a sub-component within the larger window assembly system.

subject: Window Screen
rationale: A window screen is typically a mesh panel contained within or mounted to a window frame, forming part of the window assembly.

subject: Window Screen
rationale: The window screen sits adjacent to the window sash, either on the interior or exterior side, covering the openable portion of the window.

subject: Window Screen
rationale: The screen is mounted into or adjacent to the window frame structure that holds it in place.

subject: Window Screen
rationale: The bottom edge of the window screen often rests on or connects to the window sill for support and sealing.

subject: Window Screen
rationale: The screen mesh panel is typically enclosed or bordered by the window frame or a separate screen frame.

subject: Window Screen
rationale: Window screens on operable windows are accessible from the interior for cleaning, removal, or replacement.

subject: Window Screen
rationale: The window screen is located in the plane of the exterior wall opening where the window is installed.

subject: Kick Plate
rationale: A kick plate is typically installed at the bottom of a door to protect it from scuffs and kicks.

subject: Kick Plate
rationale: The kick plate sits at the bottom of the door within the door frame, adjacent to the frame edges.

subject: Vision Panel / Door Lite
rationale: A vision panel or door lite is a glazed window component installed within a door leaf.

subject: Vision Panel / Door Lite
rationale: The vision panel is set within the door, and the door is mounted within the door frame, making them adjacent through the door assembly.

subject: Vision Panel / Door Lite
rationale: The vision panel/lite is physically enclosed within the door leaf material (e.g., wood, metal, or fiberglass).

subject: Vision Panel / Door Lite
rationale: The vision panel provides visual connectivity between interior spaces or between interior and exterior through the door.

subject: Window Opening Restrictor
rationale: The window opening restrictor is physically attached to the window frame to limit how far the window can open.

subject: Window Opening Restrictor
rationale: The restrictor is mounted adjacent to or on the window sash, interacting with it to restrict movement.

subject: Window Opening Restrictor
rationale: The restrictor is positioned above the window sill as part of the window assembly.

subject: Window Opening Restrictor
rationale: The window opening restrictor is a component enclosed within the larger window assembly system.

subject: Lift Car
rationale: A lift car physically travels within and is enclosed by the lift shaft.

subject: Lift Car
rationale: In many traction elevator configurations, the machine room is located above the lift shaft, placing the lift car below it when at upper floors.

subject: Lift Car
rationale: The lift car sits above the lift pit at the bottom of the shaft when at the lowest floor level.

subject: Lift Shaft
rationale: Lift shafts are typically located within or adjacent to the vertical circulation core of a building, alongside stairs and other lifts.

subject: Lift Shaft
rationale: A lift shaft physically contains the lift car that moves up and down within it.

subject: Lift Shaft
rationale: The lift pit is a recessed area below the lowest floor level of the lift shaft; the shaft extends above the pit.

subject: Lift Shaft
rationale: The lift machine room (or overhead) is typically located directly above the lift shaft to house the hoisting machinery.

subject: Lift Shaft
rationale: The lift shaft is enclosed by the building's structural walls and floors, forming a vertical chase through the building.

subject: Lift Shaft
rationale: Lift shafts are often placed adjacent to stairwells as part of the building's egress and vertical circulation strategy.

subject: Lift Machine Room
rationale: Lift machine rooms are typically located directly adjacent to or on top of the elevator shaft they serve, sharing a common wall.

subject: Lift Machine Room
rationale: In many building designs, the lift machine room is positioned directly above the elevator shaft (overhead machine room configuration).

subject: Lift Machine Room
rationale: The lift machine room houses the elevator controller, drive systems, and other control equipment necessary for lift operation.

subject: Lift Machine Room
rationale: There is a physical connection via cable/rope openings and possibly a door between the machine room and the elevator shaft.

subject: Lift Machine Room
rationale: Lift machine rooms are sometimes located adjacent to stairwells on mechanical floors for maintenance access, though this varies by design.

subject: Lift Pit
rationale: The lift pit is situated at the bottom of the lift shaft and is enclosed by the shaft walls.

subject: Lift Pit
rationale: The lift pit is physically continuous with the lift shaft, forming its lower termination.

subject: Lift Pit
rationale: The lift pit typically sits on or is formed within the building's foundation slab at the lowest level.

subject: Lift Pit
rationale: The lift pit houses buffer springs or hydraulic buffers that serve as safety stops at the bottom of the lift travel path.

subject: Lift Guide Rails
rationale: Lift guide rails are typically installed inside the lift shaft to guide the elevator car.

subject: Lift Guide Rails
rationale: Guide rails interact with the lift car via guide shoes to ensure smooth vertical movement.

subject: Lift Guide Rails
rationale: Guide rails extend below the lift car within the shaft pit to provide stability and emergency braking guidance.

subject: Lift Guide Rails
rationale: Guide rails are mounted within the shaft and extend into the pit area, positioned above the pit floor.

subject: Lift Counterweight
rationale: The lift counterweight is mechanically connected to the elevator car via cables and pulleys in a traction elevator system.

subject: Lift Counterweight
rationale: The counterweight travels within the elevator shaft alongside the elevator car.

subject: Lift Counterweight
rationale: In typical configurations, when the elevator car is at the top, the counterweight is at the bottom of the shaft, and vice versa, but they move in opposite directions.

subject: Lift Counterweight
rationale: The counterweight is guided by vertical guide rails that keep it aligned within the shaft.

subject: Lift Counterweight
rationale: The counterweight is enclosed within the elevator shaft structure.

subject: Lift Hoisting Ropes or Belts
rationale: Lift hoisting ropes or belts are physically located within the lift shaft, running from the machine room to the elevator car.

subject: Lift Hoisting Ropes or Belts
rationale: The ropes or belts are attached to the elevator car to lift and lower it within the shaft.

subject: Lift Hoisting Ropes or Belts
rationale: The hoisting ropes are attached at the top of the elevator car, positioned above it within the shaft.

subject: Lift Traction Machine
rationale: The lift traction machine is typically mounted adjacent to or directly above the lift car's travel path, sharing the same hoistway or machine room.

subject: Lift Traction Machine
rationale: In many traction elevator configurations, the machine is positioned above the lift car, typically in an overhead machine room.

subject: Lift Controller
rationale: The lift controller is usually positioned adjacent to or near the elevator shaft to minimize cable length and control latency.

subject: Lift Controller
rationale: The lift controller is electrically and logically connected to the elevator car for motor control, floor selection, and door operations.

subject: Lift Controller
rationale: In many installations, the main controller is located at the ground or basement level, below the elevator car's travel path.

subject: Lift Landing Doors
rationale: Lift landing doors interface with the lift car doors and provide access between the lift landing and the lift car when opened.

subject: Lift Landing Doors
rationale: The lift landing doors are part of the lift shaft enclosure, mounted on the shaft wall opening at each floor level.

subject: Lift Landing Doors
rationale: Lift landing doors are typically accessed directly from a corridor or lobby on each floor.

subject: Lift Buffers
rationale: Lift buffers are located at the bottom of the elevator shaft, physically adjacent to the shaft walls.

subject: Lift Buffers
rationale: Lift buffers are positioned at the base of the shaft below the elevator car to absorb impact in case of over-travel.

subject: Lift Car Doors
rationale: Lift car doors are physically mounted on and part of the lift car assembly.

subject: Lift Car Doors
rationale: Lift car doors interface and synchronize with landing doors at each floor for safe passenger transfer.

subject: Lift Car Doors
rationale: The car doors are adjacent to and move within the lift shaft.

subject: Lift Safety Gear
rationale: Lift safety gear is typically mounted on or within the lift car structure as a safety mechanism.

subject: Lift Safety Gear
rationale: The safety gear engages with the guide rails to brake or stop the lift car during emergencies.

subject: Lift Safety Gear
rationale: In many elevator configurations, the safety gear is located beneath the lift car.

subject: Lift Overhead Beam
rationale: The lift overhead beam is typically positioned above the lift car within the elevator shaft, providing structural support.

subject: Lift Overhead Beam
rationale: The overhead beam is located at the top of the shaft near or adjacent to the lift machine room which houses the hoisting machinery.

subject: Lift Overhead Beam
rationale: The overhead beam often provides top anchorage or support points for the lift guide rails within the shaft.

subject: Lift Overhead Beam
rationale: The overhead beam is at the highest point of the lift shaft, opposite the lift pit at the bottom.

subject: Lift Traveling Cable
rationale: The lift traveling cable connects the lift car to the control system, providing power and communication.

subject: Lift Traveling Cable
rationale: The traveling cable is housed within the lift shaft (hoistway) along its vertical run.

subject: Lift Traveling Cable
rationale: The traveling cable runs alongside the guide rails within the lift shaft.

subject: Lift Traveling Cable
rationale: The traveling cable typically loops beneath the lift car to allow for vertical movement.

subject: Lift Call Buttons and Indicators
rationale: Call buttons are positioned next to lift landing doors on each floor to allow passengers to summon the elevator.

subject: Lift Call Buttons and Indicators
rationale: The call buttons and indicators are electrically wired to the lift controller, sending signals for floor requests and receiving status updates for display.

subject: Hydraulic Lift Ram and Cylinder
rationale: The ram and cylinder mechanism is directly connected to the lift car platform, typically positioned adjacent or directly beneath the car to provide vertical motion.

subject: Hydraulic Lift Ram and Cylinder
rationale: The ram and cylinder assembly is typically installed within the lift shaft (hoistway), enclosed by the shaft structure.

subject: Hydraulic Lift Ram and Cylinder
rationale: Buffers (spring or oil buffers) are often positioned adjacent to the cylinder base in the pit as safety devices.

subject: Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Shielding for Lift Shaft
rationale: EMI shielding for a lift shaft is a component that is installed within or encloses the lift shaft structure itself.

subject: Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Shielding for Lift Shaft
rationale: The EMI shielding surrounds the lift shaft, which houses the lift car, so it has a shielding relationship with the moving lift car inside.

subject: Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Shielding for Lift Shaft
rationale: The lift shaft (and its EMI shielding) is adjacent to the surrounding building structure such as floors, walls, and slabs.

subject: Lift Emergency Phone or Intercom
rationale: The emergency phone or intercom is physically mounted inside the lift car enclosure.

subject: Lift Emergency Phone or Intercom
rationale: The intercom/emergency phone is wired or wirelessly connected to a building security or emergency response system.

subject: Auditorium/Tiered Seating
rationale: The seating area connects to the lobby/foyer via entrance points for audience access.

subject: Auditorium/Tiered Seating
rationale: Tiered seating areas are accessible from main corridors/aisles that lead to seating rows.

subject: Auditorium/Tiered Seating
rationale: When both exist, the main floor tiered seating is adjacent to balcony seating areas above.

subject: Auditorium/Tiered Seating
rationale: Tiered seating areas contain aisles/passageways between seat sections for circulation.

subject: Bleacher/Grandstand Seating
rationale: Grandstands typically connect to concourse areas for circulation and access to concessions/restrooms.

subject: Bleacher/Grandstand Seating
rationale: Spectators access seating rows from the concourse level behind or below the seating block.

subject: Bleacher/Grandstand Seating
rationale: Staircases provide vertical circulation connecting seating rows/levels to concourses and exits.

subject: Fixed Bench Seating
rationale: In some transit configurations, fixed bench seating is enclosed by a bus shelter structure.

subject: Fixed Individual Seat
rationale: Fixed individual seats are typically accessible from a nearby aisle for entry and exit.

subject: Fixed Booth Seating
rationale: Fixed booth seating is part of and enclosed within the auditorium space.

subject: Fixed Booth Seating
